page.layout: One page of running text, with two marginal notes in the right margin. The notes are "III." beside the Argumentum paragraph and "Ludi progy-mnastici militia." beside the Progymnastici line. Running head at top, page number at top right, signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: lusu substituit, luctam, discum, cursum, saltum, cestum.
Addatur restrictio Imperatoris: Sed nec permittimus etiam in his ludere ultra unum solidum, etiamsi multum dives sit: ut si quem vinci contigerit, casum gravem non sustineat.

Argumentum III. seu III. genus ludo-III.rum licitorum: Progymnastici militia.Ludi progy-mnastici militia. Exponantur aliqui veteribus usitati: Saltatio Pyrrhica: certamen equestre vel currule: ναυμαχία: Et hodie: Palastrica: jaculatoria, &c.
Accommodentur etiam his conditiones: ne sint 1. lucrosi. 2. Immoderati. 3. Intempestivi. 4. periculosi.

Probetur sic esse licitos: 1. Quia sunt exercitia tractandorum armorum civibus & Reipub. utilia & necessaria ad defensionem. Maior probetur: quia ipsa militia: & defensio Reipub. est licita. Minor exornetur a commodis peritiae armorum, ex Arist. Eth. lib. 3. c. 8. ποιῆσαι καὶ μὴ πα-θεῖν μάλιστα ἀλλ' ἀνδρικῶς [?] ... ἀπὸ τῆς ἐμπειρίας [?], &c. Et ab incommodis imperitia, ibidem.
II. quia excitant studium virtutis & gloriae.

p.i: Amplificetur a praemiis propositis industriam excitantibus, & victori gloriosis.

main_text.p: Per occupationem ostendatur: non esse inhonesta lucra:

1. quia proponuntur a magistratu, vel magistratus authoritate a privatis. 2. quia fere sunt vilia, ut pannus, aries, &c. olim olea, pinus, apiū, pomum. Plutarch. quaest. Symp. quaest. 3. lib. 5. & quaest. 4. lib. 8. Item Herod. lib. 8. de oleagena co-

page.notes: Greek in the Aristotle reference (Eth. III.8) is only partly legible; the marked words are doubtful. The word after "ναυμαχία" is set as printed but its exact form is uncertain. The "III." numeral in the text and the margin is printed as "III." in both places. The catchword "rona" is the first word of the next page. Long s is normalised to s throughout.
